en: Boldly let us raise our banner high!
Though the storm of hostile elements howls,
Though grim forces oppress us today,
Though tomorrow is certain for no one...
Oh!... for it is the banner of all mankind,
It is the holy watchword, the song of resurrection,
It is the triumph of labour — of justice,
It is the dawn of the brotherhood of all peoples.
Forward, Warsaw!
To the bloody fight,
Holy and just!
March, march, Warsaw!...
Today, when the working people are dying of hunger,
To drown in luxury is a crime, as in mud;
And shame on him among us who in his youth
Is afraid to stand even on the scaffold!
No one dies in vain for an idea,
In time Christ overcomes Judas!
Let holy fire seize the young,
Though many will fall — yet the future is ours!
Forward, Warsaw! etc. etc.
Hurrah!... let us tear the crowns from the tsars,
While the peoples still go in crowns of thorns;
And let us drown the half-rotten thrones in blood,
Crimsoned in the blood of the people!...
Ha!... terrible vengeance on today's executioners,
Who suck the life out of millions!...
Ha!... vengeance on the tsars and plutocrats!
And the harvest of the future's crops will come!
Forward, Warsaw! etc.
notes: line 4.2: 'Zbrodnią w rozkoszy tonąć, jak w błocie' is elliptical: 'it is a crime to drown in pleasure (luxury) as in mud'.
line 4.9 and 5.9: 'itd.' (i tak dalej, 'and so on') marks the refrain of stanza 3 to be sung again; rendered 'etc.'.
line 5.2: 'chodzą w cierniowej' leaves the noun unsaid: 'go in a thorny [crown]', i.e. a crown of thorns, set against the tsars' crowns.
line 5.8: 'żniwo przyszłości plonów' = literally 'the harvest of the crops of the future'.
